monthly_review.summary: You increased volume and shifted toward more balanced intensity distribution this month, with notable gains in aerobic efficiency and cadence consistency — a sign of improved neuromuscular coordination and fatigue resilience.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved by +0.38 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift across all metrics — indicating better oxygen utilization at given heart rates.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance by 5.1 km and completed 2 more runs — no additional running is needed to match or exceed March’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite lower cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.66 m/sec per bpm even as average cadence dropped from 150 to 142 spm — suggesting improved stride economy, likely due to longer stride length (avg 77–92 cm in recent runs) and reduced vertical oscillation variability.

insights.title: Z1 volume nearly 6× higher than last month
insights.body: Zone 1 effort increased from 4% to 23% of total time — a meaningful recovery and base-building shift, especially visible in the 14:00/km recovery run on 2026-04-26 (HR 120 bpm, cadence 87 spm).

insights.title: Cadence inconsistency under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence ranged from 87 spm (2026-04-26, HR 120) to 150 spm (2026-04-22, HR 143), with lowest values occurring during slowest paces — suggesting form breakdown or intentional walk-run strategy rather than fatigue-driven inefficiency.

insights.title: Z4 time up 25% but Z5 remains minimal
insights.body: Zone 4 effort rose from 12% to 15% of total time, while Zone 5 stayed flat at 4% this month vs 1% last — indicating purposeful introduction of threshold work without overreaching into VO2 max territory.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a 5 km Zone 2 steady-state effort targeting HR 130–138 bpm and cadence ≥145 spm to reinforce aerobic efficiency gains observed this month.
recommendations.reason: Your April avg HR was 142 bpm with declining cadence (142 spm vs March’s 150); locking in Zone 2 at lower HR with higher cadence will strengthen neuromuscular patterning and efficiency.

recommendations.action: Repeat the 3.1 km session from 2026-04-22 (7:08/km, HR 143, cadence 150, ground contact 298 ms) as a benchmark interval — aim to hold same pace with HR ≤141 bpm and ground contact ≤295 ms.
recommendations.reason: This session showed optimal balance of speed, efficiency (stride 91.8 cm), and low impact (298 ms GCT); replicating it will test aerobic power consolidation.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-sec strides at 4:28/km (best pace from data) post-warmup on one easy run this week, focusing on vertical oscillation ≤8.0 cm and cadence ≥152 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your best pace (428 sec/km) occurred with VO2 max 36.0 and vertical oscillation 8.2 cm — reducing bounce slightly while increasing turnover will sharpen race-specific neuromuscular recruitment.

weekly_focus.description: Consolidate recent aerobic efficiency gains by reinforcing optimal cadence-stride-GCT relationships across intensities — using HR as anchor, not pace.
suggested_sessions: 3 km easy + 2 × 30-sec strides (4:28/km, VO2 max pacing)
